theory.target: Test whether the fixed-basepoint hypothesis can be dropped from the ordinary H1 Borel-quotient splitting for cyclic rotations of a circle; distinguish a homotopy quotient from the coarse quotient.
definitions: C_m rotates the oriented N=mL-edge CW circle by kL cells,0<=k<m.
X_hC_m is the Borel homotopy quotient, distinct from the coarse orbit space.
A group-fixed point is fixed by every element; trivial H1 action is weaker.
Homology is ordinary integral homology; Z/1 denotes zero.
A primitive free covector kills all relations and has coefficient gcd1.
assumptions: Ordinary integral homology of a connected oriented cyclic CW graph with N=m*L vertices and edges; N=2 is a two-edge CW circle, not an abstract simplicial complex.
The generator of C_m sends vertex/edge v to v+k*L modulo N, 0<=k<m; no edge reversals.
The normalized group-bar complex tensored with cellular chains models ordinary homotopy-orbit chains. The chain computation through degree2 is sufficient only for H1.
A group-fixed point is stronger than trivial action on H1. No A1-localization or Nisnevich-sheaf comparison is assumed.
Universal topological and motivic bridges require independent review; no parent solution or novelty claimed.
approaches_considered: Lift the rotation to the universal cover while retaining its group label, derive a two-generator extension presentation and integral gcd profile.
Track degree-one graded pieces and the abutment extension; test whether trivial monodromy supplies a section.
Compute normalized bar/cellular boundaries and integral H1 independently, beginning with free, fixed-point and nonfaithful controls.
falsification_targets: Trivial H1 action substitutes for a group-fixed basepoint.
Every homotopy quotient can be replaced by its coarse quotient.
The proposed gcd profile or primitive fiber covector fails in a bounded case.

claims.statement: Trivial action on ordinary H1 can replace a group-fixed basepoint in the proposed H1 Borel splitting. Refuted by the half-turn circle: H1=Z, not Z direct-sum C2, and the fiber has free coordinate2.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong finite chain complex, invalid integral reduction, nontrivial induced H1 action, or wrong primitive fiber coordinate.

claims.statement: Every cyclic rotation has the same H1 for its Borel and coarse quotients. Refuted by the trivial C2 action: Borel H1=Z direct-sum C2 whereas the coarse quotient is a circle.
claims.falsification_condition: Failure of the trivial-action product model, wrong integral H1 calculation, or a non-circle coarse quotient.

claims.statement: For all m>=2,0<=k<m,L>=1, the ordinary Borel H1 of rotation by k/m is Z direct-sum Z/gcd(m,k), from the presentation k*t+m*b=0; the fiber maps to m/gcd(m,k) in its primitive free quotient.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed lifting interpretation, discarded stabilizer, incorrect integral basis change, or a counterexample outside the finite domain.

claims.statement: Two methods agree on60 profiles for20 rotation actions under3 subdivisions;11004 d1*d2 column identities pass and45 profiles fail the weakened splitting formula.
claims.falsification_condition: A missing input, wrong incidence column, nonintegral elimination or profile mismatch.

claims.falsification_condition: A nonprimitive or nonannihilating covector accepted, wrong fiber value, targeted mutation accepted, or replay hash mismatch.

claims.statement: AIM Question9 asks a broader Morel A1-homology spectral-sequence question than the imported finite-group specialization; Brown Definition5.1 and Example5.2(c) distinguish ordinary Borel homology from coarse quotient homology, the latter requiring free action.
claims.falsification_condition: Wrong primary-source locator, visual transcription error, or omitted freeness hypothesis.

claims.statement: The ordinary fixed-point audit does not establish the imported A1-local spectral sequence, its strong convergence, or its fixed-basepoint splitting theorem. A comparison with the intended motivic category is still required.
claims.falsification_condition: An independently checked comparison theorem with all hypotheses supplied would close this stated gap.

progress.summary: A free half-turn has trivial H1 action but H1 Borel=Z, with fiber coordinate2; the fixed-point weakening fails. The trivial-action control also rejects a nonfree coarse-quotient substitution.
Visual reading recovers the damaged AIM notation without altering the frozen bytes; ordinary primary references delimit Borel versus free quotient homology.
